title: Applying for a Camp Job
shared_passage:
Listen to Philip speaking to Rose Jasper at an interview for a job at a children's camp. For questions 1 to 8, decide whether the statements are true or false.

ROSE: Good afternoon; I'm Rose Jasper. How do you do?
PHILLIP: How do you do? Philip West.
ROSE: Nice to meet you, Philip. Please, have a seat. So, you are applying for the job of activity leader at our children's summer camps. Do you have any experience of working with children?
PHILLIP: Yes, I do. When I was at school, I volunteered with my local soccer club. I assisted at practice sessions, and I was responsible for communicating the dates and times of matches to the children and their families, and I made sure the children were safe.
ROSE: Great! So what problems did you have in your role as a volunteer, and how did you deal with these problems?
PHILLIP: Mm, one of the big problems was motivation. Sometimes children wanted to leave the club, and when one child left, their friends wanted to leave too. I solved this problem in different ways. First, I made sure the children enjoyed the soccer sessions. I encouraged them and praised them for their progress. I told jokes and gave the kids attention. Because of me, some children decided not to quit. I was happy about that.
ROSE: Well done! Those are very useful skills. Now, at the camp, you will have to work long hours. Do you have experience with that?
PHILLIP: Yes, I do. In my summer holidays last year, I worked in a factory as a machine operator. I wanted to earn money, so I did a lot of overtime. It wasn't interesting work, but I didn't mind that.
ROSE: That's good to know. Now, as an activity leader, it's important to have a good relationship with your co-workers. Do you work well with other people?
PHILLIP: Yes, I enjoy working in a team, and I always get on with my co-workers. For example, at the factory, I helped my colleagues when they were busy, and I was always motivated and positive. Plus, I always followed instructions from my boss without complaining, even when the work was hard.
ROSE: Great. Well, thank you for your time, Philip. I'll be in touch.

questions.question: Philip is applying for a job as an activity leader.
Philip worked as a teacher in a school.
Philip was responsible for communicating to team members.
Philip quit the team because he did not get enough praise and encouragement.
Philip worked long hours when he worked at a factory.
Philip thought the work at the factory was interesting.
Philip's co-workers at the factory helped him a lot.
Some of Phillip's co-workers at the factory were often complaining to the boss.
